text:
maria: ran an nsys trace against the v2-serving job (replica=4) to investigate the latency spike. looks like repeated cublasLt workspace allocations + 'cublasLtMatmul' fallbacks for the 1536x4096 matmuls. timeline attached (nsys).

maria: sample nsys snippet:```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=matmul_fallthrough ./run_inference.sh --mode=loadtest
# timeline shows ~90% of matmul time in workspace query/alloc kernels, then algo fallback kernel execs```

jon: can you paste the kernel timeline text? small screenshots get lost.

maria: pasted the highlights:```
[GPU] 00:00:12.345 cublasLtGetWorkspaceSize (query) 0.8ms
[GPU] 00:00:12.346 cudaMalloc (workspace) 2.4ms
[GPU] 00:00:12.349 cublasLtMatmul (algo A) 0.6ms
[GPU] 00:00:12.950 cublasLtMatmul (algo fallback B) 9.3ms
[repeat] workspace alloc + fallback per small batch element -> spikes
```

sophia: that pattern screams workspace thrash. algo probe picks algo A (fast) but workspace insufficient so cuBLASLt falls back to algo B with higher time. the alloc/free roundtrip kills latency.

kevin: +1. we saw similar in prod when sequence length distribution shifts because KV cache warmup temporarily increases effective seq_len. small batches that used algo with large workspace end up forcing fallbacks.

alex: perf-bot flagged a regression yesterday: `matmul_mean_p95 +18%` for commit `a1b2c3d4`. looks correlated with recent batching heuristic change (coalesce window shrink).

perf-bot: perf-alert: matmul_mean_p95 increased 18% on staging, trace id=matmul_fallthrough_197350. Suspect: batching reduction -> fewer shapes batched -> different algo choices.

jon: two quick mitigations to test: 1) pre-allocate a workspace pool per-device for common max sizes (avoid cudaMalloc in hot path), 2) cache cublasLt algorithm selection per (shape, dtype, seq_len_bucket).

kevin: code sketch for pool (concept):```c
// one pool entry per device
void* workspace_pool[MAX_DEVICES];
size_t pool_size = 128*1024*1024; // 128MB
cudaSetDevice(d);
cudaMalloc(&workspace_pool[d], pool_size);
// when a matmul wants workspace: slice from pool, no free() in hot path
```

maria: we should also consider changing the algo selection heuristic: prefer algorithms with smaller workspace footprint at p95 latency-critical routes. keep throughput routes on default pick.

alex: agree. add a routing flag: `prefer_low_ws` for customer tiers where latency trumps token-cost. then runtime can bias cublasLt algorithm search: weight = time + alpha * (ws_bytes / WS_SCALE). tune alpha.

sophia: also worth adding a warmup pass after KV cache growth events. when a new prefix length becomes common, do a lightweight probe for top-k shapes to populate algo cache and claim workspace slices. reduces cold-probe frequency.

jon: for reproducibility, here's the nsys command we used + the perfetto-like timeline labels:```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=/tmp/matmul_fallthrough --sample=none ./run_inference.sh
# export: nsys export -f sqlite -o matmul_fallthrough.sqlite```

jon: also captured driver timeline: `cuMemAlloc` spikes align exactly with latency outliers.

kevin: we should avoid calling `cublasLtMatmul` with new workspace size per-request. instead, have a cached `cublasLtMatmulPlan` + `cublasLtMatmul` call that reuses the same workspace handle. probing only when shape unseen.

maria: what about split-k/smaller-k strategies? some algos are split-K heavy and have better perf without huge WS, could be an option for tiny batches. but watch increased reduction costs on CPU if we fall back to host sums.

alex: next steps proposal: (1) instrument histogram of shape -> workspace_size chosen (2) implement a per-device fixed pool and a fast allocator (slab) (3) add cached algo mapping keyed by (m,n,k,dtype,splitk_flag,seq_bucket) (4) add e2e test that simulates KV cache warmup sequence distribution and assert p95 < baseline.

perf-bot: perf-req: add unit test `matmul_warmup_sim` to CI. failing test should block rollout of batching-heuristic-shrink.

maria: i'll run a microbench with pool+algo-cache tomorrow and post new traces. if that solves it we can quickly roll to staging and monitor p95. :thumbsup:

sophia: fyi, also found small but relevant nvprof snippet: `cublasLtMatmul` sometimes launches a leftover kernel that does a large memcpy when workspace > 8MB, likely due to non-coalesced scratch usage. that explains the large jump from 0.6ms to 9ms.

jon: thanks everyone. if anyone has a perfetto timeline exporter script, drop it here. i'll correlate host stacks with the GPU allocs.

kevin: dropping a link to our internal workspace-pool PR template: https://redwood.internal/pulls/ws-pool-template (will open a concrete PR after the microbench).

maria: bringing this into the Tuesday perf sync. tagging @kevin @sophia for action items.

alex: reaction :eyes:

perf-bot: noted. regression ticket created: RH-3456.

maria: end of thread for now — will update with new nsys capture.
